title: Parameter-sensitive query whose text cannot change
prompt: Finance back-office screen in a vendor module: the statement is generated by the vendor's data layer and its text
cannot change. About 40 calls per hour. Query Store query_id 4410 has two plans. The plan compiled for a normal
customer (nested loops, 1 MB grant) runs in 3 ms for normal customers and about 4 minutes, with a sort spill, for a
partner account with 180k payments. The plan compiled for a partner (hash join, parallel, 900 MB grant) runs in 2 s
for partners. Whichever compiles first after a statistics update stays in cache. Measured compile time is 9 ms.
sys.query_store_query_variant has no rows for this query. Query Store is READ_WRITE.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Payments: 60M rows. Status: Settled 88%, Failed 6%, Refunded 4% (negative Amount), Pending 2%. ExternalRef is NULL for ~30%; non-NULL values are almost unique, with a few duplicates from provider retries. Partner accounts have up to 180k Settled or Refunded payments each. Settlement batches stamp the same PaidAt on 50-500 payments.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

correct_families.description: A Query Store hint adds OPTION (RECOMPILE) without a change to the statement text. At 40 calls per hour and 9 ms per compile the cost is nothing, and each call gets a plan for its own customer.

traps.why: A forced plan is right for one population and wrong for the other on every call: the partner case stays at 4 minutes, or every normal call asks for 900 MB.
OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN gives every caller the average plan, which is the small plan: the partner case stays slow.
The vendor generates the statement. A changed text is never the text that runs.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

traps.why: Clearing the cache only decides again, by chance, which plan compiles first.
traps.example_sql: ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION CLEAR PROCEDURE_CACHE;

min_improvement.basis: Provisional. Measure each population against the baseline run with the plan compiled for the other population. Neither population may get worse than with its own plan.

key.reference_notes: The contrast is the task converted from rewrite exam Q10: there the statement runs 150 times per second, a recompile per call is too expensive, and the procedure can change.
